cases.name: describes-the-code-without-proposing
failed: must use finding headings that state what is true, not topic names such as "Booking flow"
must not propose, recommend or critique: no "should" or "consider", no fix, and no label such as bug, race, risk, fragile or problem on the check-then-insert or on the email sent after the insert

cases.name: merges-parts-reading-only-contradictions
failed: must start with a Summary of five to ten lines, each naming the section it comes from
must keep the insert before the send (`lib/bookings.ts:9`, then `10-14`), as the code shows, and say that part 2 was corrected on that point
must order the findings by capability (bookings, data, email), not by part, and merge the two parts' notes on how email is tested into one place
must list question 4 under a "Not answered" section, with where part 2 looked, and not answer it

cases.name: the-obvious-answer-is-wrong
failed: must find the provider's current limits on its own pricing or documentation page and cite the page with the date read
must quote the sentence that states the limit, at most two sentences, with a link to that section's anchor (or its heading when the page has none) and its tier
must answer yes, no or not determined in one sentence, with the limit that decides it

cases.name: worlds-not-competitors
failed: must give each world at least three concrete traits (a material, a tool or object, a convention) and two pictures that were opened, with URL and licence or marked as reference only
must cite each trait stated as a fact with a quote of at most two sentences, a link to the section and its tier, taking the museum, archive or trade source over a blog, which may only be a lead
